title: Certificate bundle manifest
$comment: Frozen as schema v1 at T1's gate (PLAN.md section 7), after the contract met live data on 18 and 19 September. Uses the keyword subset implemented by tools/validate.py; an unknown keyword is an error there, never ignored. Every change since 062a245 is listed in schema/CHANGES.md with the case that forced it; a change after the freeze needs a new schema_version and a row there.
description: Everything a checker needs to accept or refuse one result, and nothing it would have to fetch: the proposal, the snapshots it cites, the registry entries it pins, the lowered proposal and the result. A bundle is self-contained on purpose, so refusing it never depends on the state of the tree it was built from. A corrupted bundle names the class it must be refused with, so a fixture that stops being refused, or starts being refused for a different reason, fails loudly.

name.description: The bundle's directory name. Free text rather than a slug: these read as names, with hyphens, and are never used as keys.

expects.description: accept for the good bundle; otherwise the one refusal class this corruption must produce.

corruption.description: Present on every corrupted bundle: what single change was made, and where. Generated, never hand-written.

of.description: Which good bundle, and which document within it, the single change was made to.

registry.description: The registry entries this bundle carries, each naming its family and file. A bundle carries its own copy, so a review on disk cannot change what a stored bundle means. A list, not a map: the canonical JSON profile forbids a dot in a key, and a family name has one.

snapshots.description: Retained response bytes, each naming the SHA-256 the proposal cites and the file holding them. A file that does not hash to its stated digest is the first thing a checker catches.
